newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police scuffle with settlers in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police scuffle with settlers in West Bank.

text.p: Israeli police scuffled with Jewish settlers on Thursday while carting away two mobile homes that residents had placed on a West Bank hill hoping to expand their enclave, witnesses said.
Israeli police said they arrested four people in the row at Mitzpe Jericho. A police spokesman said residents had tried to block police with their bodies and cars during the scuffles.

"A huge police force suddenly entered the settlement. They came to take away two mobile homes we placed here in order to expand the community," said Moshe Eyal, a resident of the settlement of 180 Jewish families.
Michael Mar-Yosef, a settler leader, said: "They pushed and shoved us. The police officers acted brutally."
Police said about 170 policemen reinforced by soldiers removed the mobile homes placed illegally on the hill. A spokeswoman said she was checking claims of police violence.
The troops used a crane to hoist the mobile homes onto flatbed trucks and carted them away. Settlers said they had placed the mobile homes on the hill two weeks ago.

Mitzpe Jericho, about 15 km (nine miles) southeast of Jerusalem, overlooks a valley known as Wadi Kelt where two Israeli women hikers were stabbed to death last week in what police suspect was a Palestinian guerrilla attack.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government has approved the expansion of several settlements in the West Bank despite Palestinian protests. Israel's groundbreaking on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March plunged peacemaking with the Arabs into crisis.
